A few usual suspects cause this.

If the child is a plain function, React re-renders it whenever the parent re-renders, no matter what props it got. Wrapping it in `React.memo` stops that, as long as the props really are the same.

But "same" often isn't true. If you pass an inline function or a new object or array as a prop, like `onClick={() => doThing()}` or `style={{color: 'red'}}`, that makes a brand new value every render. Even `React.memo` sees that as a change. The fix is to keep those steady with `useCallback` for functions and `useMemo` for objects, or just define them outside the component.

Context is another one. If the child reads from a `useContext`, it re-renders anytime that context value changes, even if none of its own props moved.

If you tell me which case fits, I can look at the actual code with you.
